### Problem: Round Trip II {#sec-df-p1-trip2}

The roads are one-way. Print a directed cycle, or report that the flights form a DAG. A cycle may have only two cities when both directions exist.

**Graph model.** Directed. Colour $1$ is gray. The cycle is the gray path from the head of a back edge back to its tail.

**Invariants.** A vertex turns black only after every outgoing flight has been tried, so an edge into a black vertex leaves the current root path. It cannot close a cycle with the vertices still on the stack.

**Approaches.**

1. **Three colours** — the form to submit.
2. **The undirected parent test on the same arcs** — it misses the direction. On a DAG that becomes cyclic once arrows are forgotten, it reports a cycle. The sample's underlying undirected graph has the triangle; a pure DAG such as $1 \to 2 \to 3$ with an extra $1 \to 3$ has a forward edge and no directed cycle.

::: {#fig-df-p1b}

#### Three colours

::: {.form-next}
Gray is $1$, black is $2$. Only gray closes a cycle. Parent pointers record the tree arc.
:::


##### Python

```{python}
def round_trip_ii(n, edges):
    adj = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]
    for u, v in edges:
        adj[u].append(v)
    color = [0] * (n + 1)
    parent = [-1] * (n + 1)
    found = []

    def go(u):
        color[u] = 1
        for v in adj[u]:
            if found:
                return
            if color[v] == 1:
                cyc = [u]
                x = u
                while x != v:
                    x = parent[x]
                    cyc.append(x)
                cyc.reverse()
                cyc.append(cyc[0])
                found.append(cyc)
                return
            if color[v] == 0:
                parent[v] = u
                go(v)
        color[u] = 2

    for s in range(1, n + 1):
        if color[s] == 0 and not found:
            go(s)
    return found[0] if found else None


FLIGHTS = [(1, 3), (2, 1), (2, 4), (3, 2), (3, 4)]
cyc2 = round_trip_ii(4, FLIGHTS)
assert valid_cycle(4, FLIGHTS, cyc2, directed=True)
assert round_trip_ii(3, [(1, 2), (2, 3), (1, 3)]) is None
assert round_trip_ii(2, [(1, 2), (2, 1)]) == [1, 2, 1] or valid_cycle(2, [(1, 2), (2, 1)], round_trip_ii(2, [(1, 2), (2, 1)]), directed=True)
```

##### C++

```cpp
vector<int> roundTripII(int n, vector<pair<int, int>>& edges) {
    vector<vector<int>> adj(n + 1);
    for (auto [u, v] : edges) adj[u].push_back(v);
    vector<int> color(n + 1), parent(n + 1, -1), cyc;
    auto go = [&](auto&& self, int u) -> void {
        color[u] = 1;
        for (int v : adj[u]) {
            if (!cyc.empty()) return;
            if (color[v] == 1) {
                for (int x = u; x != v; x = parent[x]) cyc.push_back(x);
                cyc.push_back(v);
                reverse(cyc.begin(), cyc.end());
                cyc.push_back(cyc[0]);
                return;
            }
            if (color[v] == 0) {
                parent[v] = u;
                self(self, v);
            }
        }
        color[u] = 2;
    };
    for (int s = 1; s <= n && cyc.empty(); s++)
        if (color[s] == 0) go(go, s);
    return cyc;
}
```

:::

#### Ignore the colours

::: {.form-next}
Running the undirected test on a digraph treats a forward edge as a cycle. The three-vertex DAG $1 \to 2 \to 3$, $1 \to 3$ has no directed cycle.
:::

```{python}
assert round_trip_ii(3, dag) is None
```

##### C++

```cpp
// The undirected search of Round Trip, fed the same arcs, reports a cycle
// on the DAG 1 -> 2 -> 3, 1 -> 3. Colour 2 is what keeps that forward edge quiet.
```

:::

:::

**Worked trace.** Enter $1$, then $3$, then $2$. The flight $2 \to 1$ lands on gray. Parents give $2, 3, 1$. Reversed and closed, the route is $1, 3, 2, 1$. The flights into $4$ land on a white vertex and grow a side branch that dies without a cycle.

**Edge cases.** A single arc has no cycle. Two opposing arcs are a cycle of two cities. A self-loop is excluded by the statement (the flight joins two different cities).

**Pitfalls.** Painting a vertex black at the moment it is discovered makes every edge look like a tree edge, and the triangle is missed. Using the undirected parent test on directed flights reports the forward edge $1 \to 3$ in the DAG above.


::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistakes"}
- The undirected parent test, run on one-way flights, treats a forward edge into a black city as a cycle. On two opposing arcs it skips the flight back to the parent and prints nothing.
- The parent walk from the tail lists the cities against the arrows. Reverse it, then repeat the start.
- Resetting the colours at every start re-walks the whole graph. One colour array for the whole search is the $O(n + m)$ bound.
:::

**Variants.** The parent test belongs to @sec-df-p1-trip. A question that only asks whether a directed cycle exists is the same gray test with the route left unprinted. Listing every city that lies on some cycle needs the strongly connected components; this search only rebuilds one cycle.

Source: [CSES 1678 · Round Trip II](https://cses.fi/problemset/task/1678){.solved}
